key_insight: Eu²⁺/Eu³⁺ redox chemistry pins the Fermi level, overcoming self-limiting nitrogen incorporation in titanate-derived perovskite oxynitrides.
engineering_relevance: Fermi-level engineering offers a route to control oxynitride composition during synthesis, although solar-cell performance was not evaluated.
method: Combine theoretical modelling with experimental characterisation of titanate oxynitrides.
Vary A-site composition in Eu₁₋ₓBaₓTiO₃- and Eu₁₋ₓCaₓTiO₃-derived materials.
Use Eu redox compensation to maintain a high Fermi level during nitrogen incorporation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports nitrogen uptake up to 0.65 per formula unit by hot gas extraction, versus a self-limiting level of 0.03 in barium titanate-derived material, with Eu-associated Fermi-level pinning approximately 2.9 eV above the valence-band maximum.
watch_item: Further nitrogen incorporation remains limited by bond-angle distortion within Ti(O,N)₆ octahedra.
paper_title: Controlling nitrogen incorporation in (Eu,Ba,Ca)TiO$_3$-derived perovskite-type oxynitrides through Fermi Level Engineering
